An MP3 is small, plays everywhere and is what most podcast hosts and messaging apps expect. The export renders the whole project — every track, effect and edit — into one file.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **File → Export Audio → MP3**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Choose **File → Export audio**, set **Format** to **MP3** and press **Start export**. When the render finishes, a download link for the `.mp3` file appears in the dialog. The file is encoded in the browser; nothing leaves your computer.

## Tips

- An MP3 is a delivery copy, not a backup. Keep the project or export a WAV as well if you may edit again.
- Peaks right at full scale can clip after encoding. Normalize to −1 dB or lower before exporting.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
